rationale: The assistant landed on the correct likely cause (worn original battery pack) and sensibly handed off to Dyson once the customer declined to open anything, without unsafe instructions. However its diagnostic path was weak: it kept treating the absence of a 'solid green light' as evidence of charge failure when the V10 uses blue charging lights (which the customer reported seeing), asked the customer to run the vacuum while on the charger (not how the V10 works, and left unanswered), and never asked about declining runtime or a full direct charge. It also declared 'no further non-invasive checks' when a different socket or direct-to-battery charge were still available. The homeowner ends up in the right place but via partly incorrect reasoning.
